beats.role_note: COLD OPEN -- required fellow intro line + AI-voice disclosure; ask lands answered
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Boopesh M., and this video is about one week of fellows: what the Humanitarians AI fellows shipped into our shared YouTube repository, from October twenty-fifth to the thirty-first. A quick note: this is an AI voice reading my script. Every number comes from the git history, counted by a small script.

props.command: What did the Humanitarians AI fellows ship into humanitarians-youtube from Oct 25 to Oct 31?
output: 30 pull requests merged · busiest day: Thursday, Oct 29 (12)
37 author names → 27 people · 22 fellow folders with new work

beats.role_note: BLUF -- hesitant writer corrects the misconception
beats.narration_text: Here's the week in one line. A fellow's week isn't one big video. It's a folder of small evidence, and this week, eighty-four new folders landed.

props.text: A week of work is one big video.

contextItems.label: Evidence
contextItems.detail: README, fact check, frictional log, source

beats.role_note: 7-day bar chart of merged PRs per day, from results.json
beats.narration_text: Start with pull requests. Thirty were merged in seven days: twenty-nine merge commits, and one squash merge. Sunday and Monday had four each. Thursday, the twenty-ninth, was the busiest day, with twelve. Saturday had none. And thirty-five more commits went straight to main, without a pull request.

Who shipped it? The log shows thirty-seven author names. But one person often appears twice: a full name on one laptop, a GitHub handle on another. Merge only the obvious matches, same email or same account, and it's twenty-seven people. Twenty-three of them wrote the work. The rest only merged it. Two more pairs look alike, but I left them separate.

beats.role_note: 84 new work folders by kind (heuristic sort) + when they were dated
beats.narration_text: What did they ship? Eighty-four new work folders, from twenty-two fellows. By my rough sort: forty-two STEM explainer videos, thirty progress videos, seven renewal requests, three hours logs, and two pieces of written or code work. Twenty-seven are dated this week. Thirty-three are older work, filed this week.

beats.role_note: a few real titles as cards + the most common topic words
beats.narration_text: A few of the titles. What is R L H F? Encrypted Twice. Right Answer, Wrong Chain. Ads in the Picture. The most common topic word is physics, from one fellow's twelve-week physics engine series. After that come agents, and memory.

beats.role_note: Boopesh's own two videos; Drive submitted, GitHub PR pending (honest)
beats.narration_text: And my part. Last week I made two videos: a progress update, Brutalist, Shared, at two minutes thirteen, and a STEM explainer, Deep Hedging, at two thirty-three. Each has a Short, and all four are 4K. They're submitted to Drive. My GitHub pull request is still pending: my fork attempt failed, so I'm asking the maintainer for access. That's why my folder isn't in these numbers yet.

beats.role_note: the concrete takeaway: what a good weekly folder contains
beats.narration_text: So here's the takeaway. Small weekly evidence adds up. A good weekly folder is small and complete: a README with the result, a fact check, a frictional log of what resisted, and the source that rebuilds the video. Seventy-two frictional logs landed this week alone.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF -- prompt read aloud and explained
beats.narration_text: Your turn. With your own repository open, paste this into Claude. Read my git log for the last seven days, and turn it into a five-beat outline for a progress video: what I shipped, what's still pending, and what's missing. A good answer cites the commit hashes, and says plainly what isn't merged yet.

props.command: Read my git log for the last 7 days and turn it into a 5-beat progress-video outline: what I shipped, what's still pending, what's missing. Cite the commit hashes.

beats.narration_text: One week of fellows. With Boopesh M., for Humanitarians AI. Thanks for watching.
